newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Power has no plans to contest NRC fine.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Power has no plans to contest NRC fine.

text.p: Illinois Power Co said Monday it has no plans at this time to contest a $110,000 fine proposed by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Earlier today, the NRC said it proposed a $110,000 fine against Illinios Power for failing to correct maintenance problems with safety-related circuit breakers at the Clinton nuclear power station. The plant is located near Clinton, Ill.
"At this time, we have no plans to contest the fine," said Illinois Power spokesman John Dewey.
The NRC first informed Illinois Power of the potential violations in March at an enforcement conference at which time, the company presented its side, Dewey told Reuters.

Since that conference, Illinois Power has taken a number of steps to address the concerns including increasing the frequency of preventive maintenance, and establishing a team whose job is to monitor the breakers, Dewey said.

The company was cited for failing to take adequate corrective action to ensure the circuit breakers were adequately maintained and to prevent the use of incorrect lubricants and cleaning agents on the circuit breakers, according to an NRC news release.
Using incorrect lubricants and cleaning materials resulted in hardened grease which subsequently caused the circuit breakers to fail to operate, the NRC said.
Illinois Power, a subsidiary of Illinova Corp, has until August 31 to pay the fine or to protest it.
